root.name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Barmen Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nf3 d5 4. Nc3 Nbd7

overview: Black develops the queen's knight to d7 behind the d5 pawn, the Cambridge Springs/Westphalia family set-up, so that ...c6 and ...Bb4 or ...Qa5 can follow. White usually plays 5.Bg5 or 5.Bf4 or 5.cxd5 with a Carlsbad-type exchange. Play is slow and manoeuvring around the d4/d5 pawns, with Black solid and slightly passive.

white_ideas.idea: Pin or pressure the f6 knight with Bg5 or Bf4
Exchange on d5 for a minority attack
Keep e3 and Bd3, castle, and expand with e4 later

black_ideas.idea: Support d5 with ...c6 and ...Be7, then castle
Counter the pin with ...Bb4 or ...Qa5 (Cambridge Springs) where it fits

typical_structures.structure: QGD centre with pawns on d4/c4 against d5/e6 and tension in the centre
Carlsbad structure after cxd5 exd5 (when White exchanges)

character.notes: Standard QGD slow, positional play with a sound, slightly passive Black set-up.

structure.notes: Centre stays in tension as in the QGD.

level.notes: Standard QGD understanding, several set-ups to choose between.

sublines_that_differ.name: Cambridge Springs
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Nbd7 5. e3 c6 6. Nf3 Qa5
sublines_that_differ.how: Sharper, with an immediate queen sortie and tactics against the Bg5 pin.

character.reason: The QGD is hard to break down and the d7 knight adds a compact set-up.

gambit.reason: The c4 pawn is not a gambit; no material offered.

structure.reason: Centre in tension with d4/d5 held, as in the QGD anchor.

level.reason: Plans are known but the structures need understanding.

plans.reason: Exchange lines lead to the Carlsbad structure.
